column1: # JLPT grammar points by level - local reference table.
# The JLPT has published no official list since the 2010 overhaul: the levels
# here are settled by consensus, and each level holds at most its usual share
# of the 110 / 250 / 450 / 650 points counted from N5 up; N1 holds the rest.
# The rule name is the identity of the point: the card carries it in its `Rule`
# field and its tag, and the deck is compared on it. It is therefore unique,
# Japanese, and holds no space. A form that heads several points carries its
# grammatical category in full-width brackets: のに（逆接）, のに（目的）.
# The tier says how central the point is within its level: 1 its backbone,
# 2 common, 3 finer, rarer or more formal. The lines of a level are in the
# order `kotogen grammar jlpt` offers them: tier by tier, the most frequent
# points first, and never a point before one of its level it rests on - which
# may bring a point up ahead of its tier (な形容詞 before な形容詞＋名詞). A line
# added by hand goes at the end of its tier.
